metadata.title: Arbitrage Pricing Theory
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: Registry metadata.json expects Ross 1976 'The Arbitrage Theory of Capital Asset Pricing' (the original APT paper), but the PDF/text in source/ is the Huberman & Wang (2005) review article 'Arbitrage Pricing Theory' (Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report no. 216), written for the New Palgrave Dictionary of Economics, surveying APT including Ross's contribution.

nodes.name: Factor Model of Returns
nodes.statement: The $n \times 1$ vector $r$ of single-period random returns satisfies $r = \mu + \beta f + e$, where $f$ is a $k \times 1$ vector of factors, $\beta$ is an $n \times k$ matrix of factor loadings, and $e$ is an $n \times 1$ vector of idiosyncratic noise.
nodes.statement_clean: Each asset's return decomposes into a mean, a linear combination of factor realizations, and idiosyncratic noise.

nodes.name: Factor model equation
nodes.statement: $r = \mu + \beta f + e$, with normalization $E[f] = 0$ and $E[e] = 0$, so that $E[r] = \mu$.

nodes.name: Approximate Arbitrage Pricing Inequality
nodes.statement: There exists a constant $a$ such that for each $n$, $(\mu - X\lambda)^\top Z^{-1} (\mu - X\lambda) \leq a$ for some $(k+1) \times 1$ vector $\lambda$ and positive definite matrix $Z$, where $X = (\imath, \beta)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected returns are approximately a linear function of the factor loadings, with mean-squared pricing error uniformly bounded.

nodes.name: Approximate APT inequality
nodes.statement: $(\mu - X\lambda)^\top Z^{-1} (\mu - X\lambda) \leq a$ with $X = (\imath, \beta)$.

nodes.name: Exact Arbitrage Pricing Relation
nodes.statement: $\mu = X\lambda = \imath \lambda_0 + \beta \lambda_1$, where $\lambda_0$ is the risk-free return and $\lambda_1$ is the vector of risk premia on the $k$ factors.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected returns are exactly linear in the factor betas, with intercept equal to the risk-free rate.

nodes.name: Exact APT pricing equation
nodes.statement: $\mu = \imath \lambda_0 + \beta \lambda_1$.

nodes.name: Arbitrage (Huberman 1982)
nodes.statement: A sequence of capital markets admits arbitrage if there is a subsequence $\{w\}$ of zero-cost portfolios with $\lim_{n \to \infty} E[w^\top r] = \infty$ and $\lim_{n \to \infty} \mathrm{var}[w^\top r] = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Arbitrage = costless portfolios whose expected income diverges while their risk vanishes as the asset universe grows.

nodes.name: Arbitrage limits
nodes.statement: $\lim_{n \to \infty} E[w^\top r] = \infty$ and $\lim_{n \to \infty} \mathrm{var}[w^\top r] = 0$.

nodes.name: Well-Diversified Portfolio
nodes.statement: A portfolio $w$ is well diversified if $w^\top \imath = 1$ and $\mathrm{var}[w^\top e] = 0$. A sequence $\{w\}$ is well diversified if $w^\top \imath = 1$ and $\lim_{n \to \infty} \mathrm{var}[w^\top e] = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: A portfolio whose return is driven only by factor variation, with idiosyncratic risk eliminated.

nodes.name: Stochastic Discount Factor (SDF)
nodes.statement: The random variable $M = (\partial u / \partial c_T) / (\partial u / \partial c_0)$ satisfying $E[rM] = \imath$, named SDF by Hansen and Jagannathan.
nodes.statement_clean: Marginal rate of substitution between terminal and initial consumption that prices all assets via $E[rM]=\imath$.

nodes.name: First-order condition for SDF
nodes.statement: $E[rM] = \imath$, where $M = (\partial u / \partial c_T)/(\partial u / \partial c_0)$.

nodes.name: SDF-derived pricing decomposition
nodes.statement: $\mu = \imath \lambda_0 + \beta \lambda_1 + \alpha$ with $\lambda_0 = 1/E[M]$, $\lambda_1 = -E[fM]/E[M]$, $\alpha = -E[eM]/E[M]$.

nodes.name: Investor's Utility Maximization
nodes.statement: $\max_{c_0, c_T, w} E[u(c_0, c_T)]$ subject to $c_0 \leq b - w^\top \imath$ and $c_T \leq w^\top r$, where $b$ is initial wealth and $u$ is increasing in both consumption arguments.

nodes.name: Huberman's APT Bound (diagonal covariance)
nodes.statement: If the factor model holds and $E[ee^\top]$ is diagonal and uniformly bounded for all $n$, then absence of arbitrage implies the APT inequality $(\mu - X\lambda)^\top (\mu - X\lambda) \leq a$ with $Z = I$ and finite $a$.
assumptions: No-arbitrage in the sense of Huberman (1982)
conclusions: There exists finite $a$ such that $(\mu - X\lambda)^\top (\mu - X\lambda) \leq a$ with $Z=I$

nodes.name: Proof of Huberman's APT bound (sketch)
nodes.statement: By contradiction: if the bound fails, the orthogonal projection of $\mu$ on $\mathrm{span}(X)$ leaves a residual $\alpha$ whose squared norm diverges along a subsequence; rescaling $\alpha$ produces zero-cost portfolios satisfying the arbitrage definition.

nodes.name: Set up orthogonal projection
nodes.statement: Project $\mu$ on the column space of $X$: $\mu = X\hat\lambda + \alpha$ with $\alpha^\top X = 0$ and $\hat\lambda \in \mathbb{R}^k$. This gives $\alpha^\top \alpha = \min_\lambda (\mu - X\lambda)^\top (\mu - X\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Identify failure as divergent residual
nodes.statement: A violation of the APT inequality is the existence of a subsequence $\{\alpha^\top \alpha\}$ that approaches infinity.

nodes.name: Construct zero-cost portfolio from pricing error
nodes.statement: For any scalar $h$, set $w = h\alpha$; this portfolio has zero cost since the first column of $X$ is $\imath$ and $\alpha^\top \imath = 0$.

nodes.name: Compute mean and variance of the portfolio
nodes.statement: $E[w^\top r] = h(\alpha^\top \alpha)$ and $\mathrm{var}[w^\top r] = h^2 \alpha^\top E[ee^\top] \alpha \leq h^2 (\alpha^\top \alpha) \sigma^2$, where $\sigma^2$ is the upper bound on the diagonal entries.

nodes.name: Choose scaling to satisfy arbitrage limits
nodes.statement: Setting $h = (\alpha^\top \alpha)^{-2/3}$ gives $E[w^\top r] = (\alpha^\top \alpha)^{1/3} \to \infty$ and $\mathrm{var}[w^\top r] \leq (\alpha^\top \alpha)^{-1/3}\sigma^2 \to 0$, contradicting no-arbitrage.

nodes.name: Exact APT for Well-Diversified Portfolios
nodes.statement: Suppose there are $m > k+1$ sequences of well-diversified portfolios with matrix $W$. The exact APT holds in the limit for them iff there exist $k \times 1$ vectors $\{\lambda\}$ such that $\lim_{n \to \infty}(W^\top \mu - \tilde X\lambda)^\top (W^\top \mu - \tilde X \lambda) = 0$, where $\tilde X = (\tilde \imath, W^\top \beta)$.
assumptions: $m$ sequences of well-diversified portfolios with $m > k+1$
Each column of $W$ is a well-diversified portfolio
conclusions: Exact APT holds in the limit for the well-diversified portfolios iff $\lim_{n\to\infty}(W^\top \mu - \tilde X\lambda)^\top(W^\top \mu - \tilde X\lambda) = 0$

nodes.name: Proof for well-diversified portfolios
nodes.statement: If the limit fails, a subsequence of $\alpha = W^\top \mu - \tilde X \hat\lambda$ satisfies $\alpha^\top \alpha > \delta$; the portfolio $v = hW\alpha$ is costless and, with $h = (\alpha^\top W^\top E[ee^\top] W \alpha)^{-1/3}$, satisfies the arbitrage limits as $W$ is well-diversified.

nodes.name: Ingersoll's Generalization of APT Bound
nodes.statement: Under the factor model, uniform boundedness of the elements of $\beta$ and no arbitrage, the APT inequality holds with $Z = E[ee^\top]$ (not necessarily diagonal).
conclusions: $(\mu - X\lambda)^\top Z^{-1}(\mu - X\lambda) \leq a$ for $Z = E[ee^\top]$

nodes.name: Sketch of Ingersoll's argument
nodes.statement: Write $Z = U U^\top$ with $U$ nonsingular, then project $U^{-1}\mu$ on the column space of $U^{-1}X$: $U^{-1}\mu = U^{-1}X\lambda + \alpha$ with $\alpha^\top U^{-1}X = 0$; the rest mirrors the diagonal case.

nodes.name: Chamberlain-Rothschild Bound via Hilbert Space
nodes.statement: If asset prices admit no arbitrage, the APT inequality holds with $a = L d^2$ and $Z = I$, where $L$ is the maximum eigenvalue of the limit covariance matrix $E[ee^\top]$ and $d$ is the supremum of expectation-to-standard-deviation ratios over costless portfolios with at least one nonzero weight.
assumptions: Hilbert-space model of capital markets with possibly infinitely many assets

nodes.name: Chamberlain Mean-Variance Characterization
nodes.statement: Under additional assumptions (factors representable as limits of traded assets; variances of incomes on portfolios well-diversified in the limit and uncorrelated with factors converge to zero), exact arbitrage pricing holds iff there exists a well-diversified portfolio on the mean-variance frontier.
assumptions: Factors representable as limits of traded assets
Variances of incomes on portfolios well-diversified in the limit and uncorrelated with factors converge to zero
conclusions: Exact APT $\iff$ existence of a well-diversified portfolio on the mean-variance frontier

nodes.name: Bounded $\alpha^\top\alpha$ implies APT (utility setup)
nodes.statement: Substituting the factor model into the SDF first-order condition gives $(\mu - X\lambda)^\top (\mu - X\lambda) = \alpha^\top \alpha$ with $\alpha = -E[eM]/E[M]$; hence the APT inequality holds with $Z = I$ whenever $\alpha^\top \alpha$ is uniformly bounded by $a$.
assumptions: Investor solves $\max E[u(c_0, c_T)]$ with first-order condition $E[rM] = \imath$
conclusions: APT inequality $(\mu - X\lambda)^\top(\mu - X\lambda) \leq a$ with $Z = I$

nodes.name: Exact APT iff $E[eM] = 0$
nodes.statement: The exact APT $\mu = \imath\lambda_0 + \beta\lambda_1$ holds iff $E[eM] = 0$. If the SDF is a linear function of factors then $E[eM] = 0$; conversely, $E[eM] = 0$ implies existence of a linear-in-factors SDF satisfying $E[rM]=\imath$.

nodes.name: Connor's $k+1$ Fund Separation
nodes.statement: If the market portfolio is well diversified, then every investor holds a well-diversified portfolio (a $k+1$ fund separation: the funds are the factor portfolios and the risk-free asset), and any investor's first-order condition implies exact APT in competitive equilibrium.
conclusions: Every investor holds a well-diversified portfolio

nodes.name: Multi-Period Exact APT (Connor-Korajczyk)
nodes.statement: In a multi-period extension of Connor's model with constant capital assets, factor-structured cash payoffs, and a representative exponential-utility investor, exact arbitrage pricing obtains with time-varying risk premia and constant factor loadings.
assumptions: Capital assets are the same in all periods
Each period's payoffs follow a factor structure
conclusions: Exact APT holds in each period
Factor loadings are constant across periods

nodes.name: Chen-Ingersoll Sufficient Condition
nodes.statement: If a well-diversified portfolio is the optimal portfolio of some utility-maximizing investor, then that investor's first-order condition implies exact arbitrage pricing.
assumptions: Some utility-maximizing investor's optimal portfolio is well-diversified

nodes.name: Dybvig and Grinblatt-Titman Finite-Asset Bounds
nodes.statement: In finite-asset economies, explicit bounds on deviations from exact APT can be expressed as functions of per-capita asset supplies, individual bounds on absolute risk aversion, idiosyncratic risk variance, and the interest rate, under regularity (bounded support of $e$, non-increasing risk aversion, Pareto-optimal allocation for Dybvig; bounded risk-aversion quantity and existence of $k$ independent costless well-diversified portfolios for Grinblatt-Titman).
assumptions: Dybvig: idiosyncratic distribution bounded below; non-increasing absolute risk aversion; unconstrained Pareto-optimal equilibrium
Grinblatt-Titman: bound on risk-aversion quantity; existence of $k$ independent costless well-diversified portfolios
conclusions: Explicit upper bounds on $|\mu - \imath\lambda_0 - \beta\lambda_1|$ as functions of supplies, risk-aversion, idiosyncratic variance, interest rate

nodes.name: Mean-Variance Efficiency Equivalent of Exact APT (untraded factors)
nodes.statement: Assuming the factor structure and a risk-free asset, there exist $k$ traded assets such that a portfolio of them is mean-variance efficient iff the exact APT (3) holds; the sets of such $k$ traded assets can be characterized via the matrices $\beta\beta^\top$ and $E[ee^\top]$.
conclusions: Existence of $k$ traded assets whose linear combination is mean-variance efficient iff exact APT holds
Such asset sets are described by $\beta\beta^\top$ and $E[ee^\top]$
nodes.origin_citation: Grinblatt and Titman 1987; Huberman, Kandel and Stambaugh 1986

nodes.name: Time-series factor regression
nodes.statement: $r_t = \alpha + \beta f_t + e_t$, where $r_t, f_t, e_t$ are realizations in period $t$, and factors have mean $\delta$.

nodes.name: OLS estimators of factor model
nodes.statement: $\hat\mu = \frac{1}{T}\sum_t r_t$, $\hat\delta = \frac{1}{T}\sum_t f_t$, $\hat\beta = \big(\sum_t (r_t - \hat\mu)(f_t - \hat\delta)^\top\big)\big(\sum_t (f_t - \hat\delta)(f_t - \hat\delta)^\top\big)^{-1}$, $\hat\alpha = \hat\mu - \hat\beta \hat\delta$, $\hat\Omega = \frac{1}{T}\sum_t \hat e_t \hat e_t^\top$ with $\hat e_t = r_t - \hat\alpha - \hat\beta f_t$.

nodes.name: Restricted regression under exact APT
nodes.statement: $r_t = \imath \lambda_0 + \beta(f_t + \lambda_1) + e_t$.

nodes.name: Restricted maximum-likelihood estimators
nodes.statement: $\bar\beta = \big(\sum_t (r_t - \imath\bar\lambda_0)(f_t + \bar\lambda_1)^\top\big)\big(\sum_t (f_t + \bar\lambda_1)(f_t + \bar\lambda_1)^\top\big)^{-1}$; $\bar\Omega = \frac{1}{T}\sum_t \bar e_t \bar e_t^\top$ with $\bar e_t = r_t - \imath \bar\lambda_0 - \bar\beta(f_t + \bar\lambda_1)$; $\bar\lambda = (\bar X^\top \bar\Omega^{-1} \bar X)^{-1} \bar X^\top \bar\Omega^{-1}(\hat\mu - \bar\beta \hat\delta)$ with $\bar X = (\imath, \bar\beta)$.

nodes.name: Two-Step Empirical APT Test
nodes.statement: Estimate the factor-model parameters by OLS/MLE, then jointly solve the restricted MLE equations and compute the likelihood-ratio statistic for the APT pricing restriction.

nodes.name: Estimate factor model by OLS/MLE
nodes.statement: Compute $\hat\mu, \hat\delta, \hat\beta, \hat\alpha, \hat\Omega$ from $\{r_t, f_t\}$ via the OLS formulas (these are also MLE under multivariate normality with iid observations across $t$).

nodes.name: Solve restricted MLE
nodes.statement: Simultaneously solve the three coupled equations for $\bar\beta, \bar\Omega, \bar\lambda$ under the exact-APT restriction $r_t = \imath\lambda_0 + \beta(f_t + \lambda_1) + e_t$.

nodes.name: Compute likelihood-ratio statistic
nodes.statement: $LR = T(\log|\bar\Omega| - \log|\hat\Omega|)$, distributed as $\chi^2_{n-k-1}$ for large $T$; large $LR$ rejects the exact APT restriction.

nodes.name: Likelihood-ratio statistic for exact APT
nodes.statement: $LR = T(\log|\bar\Omega| - \log|\hat\Omega|) \sim \chi^2_{n-k-1}$ for large $T$.

nodes.name: Cross-Sectional Regression Test (Fama-MacBeth-style)
nodes.statement: OLS regression of estimated mean returns $\hat\mu$ on $\hat X = (\imath, \hat\beta)$, optionally augmented by asset characteristics $z$, with significance tests on the resulting risk-premium estimates.
input: (Optional) asset characteristics $z$ such as firm size
output: Tests on whether $\hat\lambda_1$ differs from zero and $\hat\lambda_2$ does not
nodes.origin_citation: Black, Jensen and Scholes 1972; Fama and MacBeth 1973; Chen, Roll and Ross 1986

nodes.name: Cross-sectional regressions
nodes.statement: $\hat\mu = \hat X\lambda + v$ or $\hat\mu = \imath \lambda_0 + \hat\beta \lambda_1 + v$; augmented form $\hat\mu = \imath\lambda_0 + \hat\beta\lambda_1 + z\lambda_2 + v$.

nodes.name: Factor Analysis / Principal Component Identification of Factors
nodes.statement: Algorithmic decomposition of the estimated covariance matrix of asset returns to recover factor loadings (factor analysis) or principal components (PCA) as proxies for the underlying APT factors.
input: Estimated covariance matrix of asset returns
nodes.origin_citation: Roll and Ross 1980; Chen 1983; Lehman and Modest 1985; Chamberlain and Rothschild 1983; Connor and Korajczyk 1985, 1986

nodes.name: Three approaches to factor specification
nodes.statement: Factors are identified by (i) algorithmic decomposition of the return covariance matrix; (ii) judgment-based selection guided by covariance patterns (e.g., size or book-to-market spread portfolios); (iii) purely judgmental selection of macroeconomic or financial variables tested ex post.

nodes.name: APT is not directly testable in isolation
nodes.statement: Because a mean-variance efficient portfolio always exists, finding (or failing to find) one neither supports nor contradicts the APT; it is only the joint factor structure plus exact pricing that yields refutable hypotheses.

nodes.name: APT does not preclude dynamic-portfolio arbitrage
nodes.statement: The APT is a one-period model and may permit arbitrage over dynamic portfolios; in particular, its SDF can be negative, which contradicts no-arbitrage in the presence of derivatives. Hence applying the APT to managed funds (which trade dynamically) is in tension with its no-arbitrage spirit.

nodes.name: Fama-French Three-Factor Application
nodes.statement: Fama and French (1993) use the equity-market return, the small-minus-big size spread, and the value-minus-growth (book-to-market) spread as factors; the resulting exact APT holds for portfolios sorted on size and book-to-market.

nodes.name: Daniel-Titman Counter-Example to Fama-French APT
nodes.statement: Daniel and Titman (1997) show that the Fama-French APT does not hold for portfolios sorted further on the estimated loadings on the Fama-French factors, providing evidence against the factor-pricing interpretation.

nodes.name: Chen-Roll-Ross Macroeconomic Factors
nodes.statement: Chen, Roll and Ross (1986) and Chan-Chen-Hsieh (1985) select macroeconomic variables (equity-index return, term-structure spread, default-premium spread, inflation, industrial-production growth, aggregate consumption growth) as APT factors and test the exact APT via cross-sectional regressions.
